use_case_and_requirements:
Workloads: (1) clinical note summarization + coding assist (chat/generation), (2) retrieval-augmented doc search (embeddings + rerank), (3) agent assist for care managers (streaming chat).

Performance targets (draft, from 2026-02-14 workshop):
- Chat/generation: p95 end-to-end latency <= 900ms for typical prompts; wants “no more than 10% p95 drift week-over-week without alert + comms.”
- Throughput: tokens/sec minimum floor per deployment (Dedicated pool) with headroom during business hours; asks for separate prefill vs decode metrics.
- Tail latency: wants p99 tracked and alerted but not paging unless sustained + customer-facing.

Change-management expectations:
- Explicit canary coverage for their pinned models (by model+version) and their target SKU(s).
- Canary-style alerts must trigger before broad rollout; wants documented gates: warn threshold vs rollback threshold.
- Wants runtime release notes (kernel/scheduler changes) and ability to opt into a “staged rollout ring” for their VPC.
- Must have a fast disable/rollback path; asks: “If p95 regresses, can you revert the kernel selection without redeploying everything?”

Observability/ops asks:
- Dashboards per model with breakdowns: queueing vs runtime execution; batch size distribution; tokens/sec.
- Alert payload needs links: dashboard, diff vs baseline, build id, kernel tag, hardware SKU, region.

Data handling:
- No customer prompts in Redwood systems (Arcadia explicitly asked how canary avoids PHI: synthetic prompt set only; no shadow traffic).
- US data residency only today; wants clarity on future regions and how baselines differ by region/SKU.

Model preferences:
- Open models preferred; wants pinned versions and clear fallback policies (if a model is degraded, fallback to a compatible variant).
internal_notes:

They referenced they do quarterly release freezes around key reporting windows and want Redwood to align on a “no risky kernel changes” window. They asked for a direct line to SRE on-call process (Rafael/Sean) for SLA response times.
